payload.claim: This new comment says `--all-files` and the commit hook "both read the index, so an untracked or unstaged fix is invisible to either." That conflates two different causes the task's own measured notes keep separate: `--all-files` only governs which *tracked paths* prek selects (it misses an untracked file, per the prek `--help` measurement cited in the spec's context), while an *unstaged* edit to an already-tracked file is invisible solely because the commit hook's own `git diff --cached` query reads staged content, nothing to do with `--all-files`'s file selection. A tracked file with unstaged edits is still one of 'all files' and would be handed to the hook; it is the hook's own index read (not `--all-files`) that misses the edit. The comment's causal attribution is wrong even though its practical conclusion (both miss the same fixes) happens to hold.
